title: Hydraulic Punching Machines, 33 to 193 Ton | NovoTech
meta_description: Hydraulic punching machines for plate, angle and flat bar: single-head HPM 30–175, double-head HPM DP, Siemens CNC punches and NC lines, holes to Ø2-1/4″.
intro: A hydraulic punching machine (hydraulic punch press) makes round, oblong and shaped holes in plate, angle, flat bar and sections with a punch and die in one stroke — faster and cleaner than drilling, with no chips. The HPM range starts with the 33 US ton HPM 30 and 44 US ton HPM 40 bench-height punches, continues with the 72 to 193 US ton HPM 65 – 175 with a 24.6″ throat for holes to Ø2-1/4″ in plate to 1-1/4″, and grows into the HPM DP double-head punches for two operators, the HPM CNC with a 120 × 20″ Siemens-controlled table for bolted steel-construction parts and the HPM / HKM NC punching and cutting lines that copy hole patterns along angles, flat bar and beams. Punches and dies interchange with the HKM ironworkers. Supplied with a CSA-approved panel and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
hero_points: HPM 30 – 175 single-station punches — 33 to 193 US tons, holes Ø1/4″ to Ø2-1/4″, throat to 24.6″
HPM DP double-head, HPM CNC with 120 × 20″ Siemens table, HPM / HKM NC feeding lines
Hydraulic stripper, press-brake tool, large-hole and section punching tools optional
hero_brand_line: NovoTech premium line — machines built in Turkey to NovoTech's specification with European hydraulic and electrical components, sold with a CSA-approved panel, 1-year warranty and parts and support in Canada.

groups.title: HPM hydraulic punching machines
groups.lead: Single-head, double-head, CNC-table and NC-line punches from 33 to 193 US tons.

faq.a: If holes are most of the work — base plates, gussets, clips, flat-bar brackets — a dedicated HPM punch has a deeper 24.6″ throat, a free table and a working height set for punching, and it can be fitted with an NC or CNC table. If you also shear angle, bar and flat and notch corners, the HKM ironworker puts all of it on one machine; the punches and dies are the same on both.

faq.q: How thick can a hydraulic punch go?
faq.a: Each model is rated for a hole diameter × thickness at its tonnage: Ø7/8″ × 3/8″ on the HPM 30, Ø1 × 13/16″ on the HPM 65, Ø1-5/8 × 1-1/4″ on the HPM 175. Larger holes in thinner plate are punched with the large-hole tool up to Ø4-7/8″ × 3/16″. The rule of thumb for mild steel is tonnage = hole circumference × thickness × 25 (US tons, inches).

faq.q: What does the CNC table do?
faq.a: The HPM CNC moves the plate under the punch on a 120 × 20″ table with X 63″ and Y 23.6″ travel at ±0.004″, so a hole pattern programmed once — by hand (MDI) or from a CAM file — repeats on every part. It is the machine for bolted steel-construction plates where every hole must line up with the mating member; an optional 3-head unit on the 115 and 175 keeps three tools ready.

faq.q: What is an NC punching and cutting line?
faq.a: An HPM punch or HKM ironworker with a 307 × 31″ NC feeding table: angles, flat bar and IPN / UPN beams are fed along the X axis to 244″ and the control copies the hole pattern at ±0.004″; on the HKM NC version the shear station then cuts the punched bar to length. It is the economical alternative to a CNC angle line for bracing, towers and ladders.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.
